limits: All numeric results come from one data set (Wage, n=3,000) and are illustrative, not benchmarks.
GAMs are additive; interactions must be added by hand or as 2-D smoothers.
Local regression degrades beyond p of about 3 or 4.
pygam has no local regression terms and has a bug requiring category codes shifted by one (In [44]).
Lab tables are only partly recoverable from extracted text.
practices: Use degree d no greater than 3 or 4 for polynomials; high d is wild near the boundary (Sec 7.1).
Use step functions only with natural breakpoints, else they miss the trend (Sec 7.2).
Prefer splines over high-degree polynomials: add knots, keep degree fixed (Sec 7.4.5).
Use natural splines to tame variance at the boundaries (Sec 7.4.3).
Place knots at uniform quantiles by requesting a df (Sec 7.4.4).
Choose df or lambda or span by cross-validation, or fix df around 4 per term in a GAM (Sec 7.4.4).
Pick the simpler smoothing spline when fits are similar (Sec 7.5.2).
Use ANOVA F-tests on nested models to choose polynomial degree or whether a GAM term is needed (Sec 7.8).
Check for empty cells in categorical terms of a logistic GAM before trusting fits (Sec 7.7.2).
